findings.source_passage: this critical act is not always unattended with the saddest and most fatal casualties
findings.why_it_matters: This understated, ironic closing sentence is a voice-defining moment — Melville's dry formality masking mortal danger. Its erasure removes the rhetorical punch and the narrator's characteristic deadpan.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence near-verbatim: 'But this critical act is not always unattended with the saddest and most fatal casualties.'

findings.source_passage: making a prodigious sensation in all directions. Nor, in general, is it possible to secure it again until the whale is fairly captured and a corpse.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Prodigious sensation in all directions' is a comic-inflated Melvillean phrase with signature rhetorical excess; the draft replaces it with plain paraphrase, losing both voice and irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'making a prodigious sensation in all directions' rather than folding the second iron's behavior into a bare clause.

findings.source_passage: All these particulars are faithfully narrated here, as they will not fail to elucidate several most important, however intricate passages, in scenes hereafter to be painted.
findings.why_it_matters: This meta-narrative sentence is interpretively significant: it signals Melville's deliberate preparation of the reader for future action and asserts the narrator's architectonic control — the chapter's whole justification. Its absence removes the self-conscious narratorial frame that anchors the chapter's purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore this closing sentence, at minimum as: 'All these particulars are narrated here as they will elucidate several important, intricate passages in scenes hereafter to be painted.'

summary: Three medium-severity failures — loss of the fatal-casualties understatement, erasure of 'prodigious sensation in all directions,' and complete omission of the closing meta-narrative sentence — collectively flatten the chapter's voice and strip its interpretive frame, triggering regeneration.
